## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

blocks.text:
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg

blocks.text:
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg

  (`readCustomRecordsOfType`) tail-caps each file at
  `kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes` (all consumers are tail consumers) —

  parameter defaults to the cap instead of coalescing, and a >cap

  session: open → first turn ~31–32s → 3.7s, no bogus compaction at

  as one batch every 250ms (32KB threshold / explicit flush) so tracing
  does not perturb the latency it measures; the log truncates per armed

blocks.text:
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG + GitHub Release
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main
  (gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- Lockfile policy (gh-1296 NG1): EVERY lockfile is committed and enforced —
  one inventory list in `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` (7 files:
  `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`, `ios/Podfile.lock`, `macos/Podfile.lock`,
  the vendored `flutter_inappwebview_macos` `Package.resolved`, both e2e
======
## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags
(release pipeline), the 2h auto-release coalesce schedule, `release:
published`, and workflow_dispatch ONLY — never on `push: [main]`. The
serialized-validation invariant is alarmed by `sm-merge-guard.yml`: every
main push must carry a tree covered by a successful dispatched
validation, else one deduplicated `sm-guard` issue files (no nightly
backstop, per the owner's directive).

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- fix(#1726): goal_builder marathon resume — reopening a multi-GB session
  no longer takes 30s–3.5min nor dead-ends in an over-window boot loop.
  Hidden-checkpoint estimator parity (the estimators now mirror the
  projection exactly — a hidden `CompactCheckpointRecord` covers nothing
  and renders no marker, so the resume budget trim fires instead of
  booting over-window); over-window resume boots instantly (the
  `localTrimValve` applies at open — 0 LM calls — instead of a
  minutes-long LM compaction pass; over-trigger-under-window keeps the
  LM boot cap per gh-1425); a boot-race wake gate defers inbox/steering
  wakes while a marathon load walks; and the boot raw-scan
  (`readCustomRecordsOfType`) tail-caps each file at
  `kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes` (all consumers are tail consumers) —
  `tailCapBytes: null` is the real unbounded deep-history opt-out (the
  parameter defaults to the cap instead of coalescing, and a >cap
  fixture proves null scans the whole file). Measured on the real 2.7GB
  session: open → first turn ~31–32s → 3.7s, no bogus compaction at
  open.
- feat(providers): StreamTrace diagnostic — `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` arms a
  per-chunk net→emit→render timing trail at
  `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log` (`USERPROFILE` fallback on Windows):
  `net` marks raw provider bytes from the socket, `emit` deltas leaving
  the adapter, `render` writes to the live surface — each line carries
  elapsed-ms, gap-to-previous, a global sequence number and a short
  detail, answering "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone
  for bursty endpoints. Off by default; lines are buffered and flushed
  as one batch every 250ms (32KB threshold / explicit flush) so tracing
  does not perturb the latency it measures; the log truncates per armed
  run. New public API: `StreamTrace`, `StreamTraceMark`,
  `StreamTraceSink` (barrel), `FileStreamTraceSink`,
  `streamTraceLogPath`, `maybeStartStreamTrace` (`io.dart`).

# Re: ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the `tailCapBytes: null` opt-out is a silent no-op

```dart
// lib/src/session/session_repo.dart
Future<List<CustomRecord>> readCustomRecordsOfType(
  SessionMetadata metadata,
  Set<String> types, {
  bool lastSegmentOnly = false,
  int? tailCapBytes = kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes, // null = unbounded
})
```

- The `final cap = tailCapBytes ?? kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes;` coalescing is **gone**; `tailCapBytes` flows straight into `_readCustomRecordsInFile`, so the previously dead `tailCapBytes == null ? 0 : …` branch in `_readCustomRecordsStreamed` is now live and reachable. {"content":"# Re: ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the `tailCapBytes: null` opt-out is a silent no-op

```dart
// lib/src/session/session_repo.dart
Future<List<CustomRecord>> readCustomRecordsOfType(
  SessionMetadata metadata,
  Set<String> types, {
  bool lastSegmentOnly = false,
  int? tailCapBytes = kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes, // null = unbounded
})
```

# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

```dart
Future<List<CustomRecord>> readCustomRecordsOfType(

})
```

## Scope note: the StreamTrace diagnostic rides this PR

Built to post-mortem exactly this incident's bursty-endpoint latency, so it ships here rather than separately (declared per review):

- `lib/src/providers/stream_trace.dart` / `stream_trace_io.dart` — the pure mark contract (`net` raw socket bytes, `emit` adapter deltas, `render` host writes; each line `t=<elapsed>ms +<delta>ms #<seq> <mark> <detail>`) and the io half: a line-buffered truncating file sink (one batched flush every 250ms, 32KB threshold, explicit `flush()`) and the env-gated installer.

{"newText":"## Unreleased

- fix(#1726): goal_builder marathon resume — reopening a multi-GB session
  no longer takes 30s–3.5min nor dead-ends in an over-window boot loop.
  Hidden-checkpoint estimator parity (the estimators now mirror the
  projection exactly — a hidden `CompactCheckpointRecord` covers nothing
  and renders no marker, so the resume budget trim fires instead of
  booting over-window); over-window resume boots instantly (the
  `localTrimValve` applies at open — 0 LM calls — instead of a
  minutes-long LM compaction pass; over-trigger-under-window keeps the
  LM boot cap per gh-1425); a boot-race wake gate defers inbox/steering
  wakes while a marathon load walks; and the boot raw-scan
  (`readCustomRecordsOfType`) tail-caps each file at
  `kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes` (all consumers are tail consumers) —
  `tailCapBytes: null` is the real unbounded deep-history opt-out (the
  parameter defaults to the cap instead of coalescing, and a >cap
  fixture proves null scans the whole file). Measured on the real 2.7GB
  session: open → first turn ~31–32s → 3.7s, no bogus compaction at
  open.
- feat(providers): StreamTrace diagnostic — `FA_STREAM_TRACE=1` arms a
  per-chunk net→emit→render timing trail at
  `~/.fah/logs/stream-trace.log` (`USERPROFILE` fallback on Windows):
  `net` marks raw provider bytes from the socket, `emit` deltas leaving
  the adapter, `render` writes to the live surface — each line carries
  elapsed-ms, gap-to-previous, a global sequence number and a short
  detail, answering "streamed x ms, rendered y ms" from the log alone
  for bursty endpoints. Off by default; lines are buffered and flushed
  as one batch every 250ms (32KB threshold / explicit flush) so tracing
  does not perturb the latency it measures; the log truncates per armed
  run. New public API: `StreamTrace`, `StreamTraceMark`,

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

## Issues/Notes

- **CI: no failed checks, no owned violations.** `ci_failures.md` reports all checks green on the rework head; there is no "Violations you must fix" table — nothing to fix or dispute there.

- Note: a harness WIP auto-save commit (`6481f2eee4`, session_repo + tail-cap test mid-edit snapshot) landed on the branch during the pass; the finished work is `3762fb3285` on top of it. No history was rewritten.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING, `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart:200`) — StreamTrace scope undocumented.** Took the reviewer's option 2 (document in place; splitting was rejected as it would churn ~400 lines out of the incident fix at rework time):
  - PR title now ends `(+ StreamTrace diagnostic)`; the description gained a "Scope note" section (what/why/file inventory/wiring) and the complete six-file test list.
  - `CHANGELOG.md`: two `## Unreleased` entries — the goal_builder resume fix and the StreamTrace public API + `FA_STREAM_TRACE` knob (repo rule: PRs add lines under `## Unreleased`).
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT, `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:842`) — `tailCapBytes: null` was a silent no-op.** Applied the suggested signature: `int? tailCapBytes = kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes // null = unbounded`, dropped the `??` coalescing so the previously dead `offset = 0` branch in `_readCustomRecordsStreamed` is live. Replaced the vacuous test with a fixture that genuinely crosses the cap: ~105MB of raw filler written directly to the session file (bypassing the storage's own hard-cap truncation), an explicit `greaterThan(kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes)` size assertion so it can never go vacuous, default call → tail record only, `tailCapBytes: null` → both records.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION, `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart:810`) — stray blank line** splitting the `AutoCompactorSources` doc comment: removed; comment is one block again.
- **Thread 4 (SUGGESTION, `bin/fah.dart:91`) — Windows never traced; doc cited a non-existent API.** New tested helper `streamTraceLogPath` in `stream_trace_io.dart` resolving `$HOME` with a `USERPROFILE` fallback (empty `HOME` falls through too); `bin/fah.dart` uses it. Doc now says real hosts pass `(key) => Platform.environment[key]`; truncation-per-armed-run documented on both `FileStreamTraceSink` and `maybeStartStreamTrace`.
- **Thread 5 (SUGGESTION, `lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart:30`) — per-mark synchronous `flush: true` on the hot stream path.** `FileStreamTraceSink` now buffers lines and lands one batched append+flush every 250ms (one-shot timer, re-armed per line; max exit linger ≤ interval), inline past a 32KB threshold, or via a new explicit `flush()`. Silent-on-failure contract unchanged; both public constructors source-compatible (new optional `flushInterval`).

TDD: threads 2/4/5 each went RED first (null-coalescing failure on the >cap fixture; compile-RED on the new API; immediate-write assertions failing against the old sink), then GREEN with the minimum change; thread 3 is comment-only.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

```dart
Future<List<CustomRecord>> readCustomRecordsOfType(
  SessionMetadata metadata,
  Set<String> types, {
  bool lastSegmentOnly = false,
  int? tailCapBytes = kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes, // null = unbounded
})
```

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.
- The silent-on-failure contract is unchanged (constructor truncate and batch write both guarded); `FileStreamTraceSink(file)` and `maybeStartStreamTrace(file, envLookup: …)` stay source-compatible, with an optional `flushInterval` for tests.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_5_buffered_sink.md"}

{"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
- The batch lands as one appended+`flush: true` write every **250ms** (one-shot timer, re-armed per buffered line — the process lingers at most one interval past the last mark), **inline** once the buffer passes **32KB** (bounds memory on a burst and keeps single writes bounded), or via the new explicit **`flush()`**.

New tests pin the contract: marks leave the file empty until the interval fires; the interval path lands them without an explicit flush; the 32KB threshold lands immediately (proven with an hour-long interval); `flush()` forces the batch. `mark()` itself remains a single null-check when the knob is off.

{"content":"# Re: ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the `tailCapBytes: null` opt-out is a silent no-op

```dart
// lib/src/session/session_repo.dart
Future<List<CustomRecord>> readCustomRecordsOfType(
  SessionMetadata metadata,
  Set<String> types, {
  bool lastSegmentOnly = false,
  int? tailCapBytes = kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes, // null = unbounded
})
```

- The `final cap = tailCapBytes ?? kSessionSegmentHardCapBytes;` coalescing is **gone**; `tailCapBytes` flows straight into `_readCustomRecordsInFile`, so the previously dead `tailCapBytes == null ? 0 : …` branch in `_readCustomRecordsStreamed` is now live and reachable. {"content":"# Re: 💡 SUGGESTION: per-chunk synchronous `flush: true` writes on the hot stream path

Done — the sink is line-buffered now (`lib/src/providers/stream_trace_io.dart`):

- `writeLine` only appends to an in-memory buffer; **no disk write per mark**.
